title: customer-penetration-test-scope-and-onboarding-template-2026
author: Asha Patel
body:
Title: Customer penetration test scope and onboarding template

Overview:
This document provides a reusable, customer-facing penetration test (pen-test) scope and onboarding template for private (VPC and on‑prem) Redwood Inference deployments. It captures the security team’s minimum acceptance criteria, scheduling and communication workflow, permitted blast radius, evidence packaging requirements, and operator remediation playbook. Use this template when customers request a third‑party pen test or when Redwood facilitates a joint test with a customer-selected vendor.

Purpose and audience:
- Purpose: accelerate and standardize customer pen-test onboarding while preserving safety of runtime and operator workflows.
- Audience: security engineers, field delivery/ops, customer security teams, and contracted third‑party testers.

Key objectives (what success looks like):
1) Test covers agreed-in-scope assets and returns a vulnerability report with severity triage and reproducible steps.
2) Attack surface constrained to explicit IP/CIDR ranges, authenticated interfaces, and non-production tenants when required.
3) All findings are validated by Redwood and the customer, with remediation timeline and verification steps.
4) Artifacts and evidence follow the data handling and retention policy described below.

Scope definition (pick one or combine):
- Option A: Customer-managed VPC (Redwood control plane separated): scope limited to customer-provided tenant endpoints, tenant-specific model endpoints, and agreed instrumentation endpoints. No control plane, operator console, or infra management endpoints are in scope unless explicitly authorized.
- Option B: On‑prem appliance / air‑gapped site: scope limited to the appliance management IP range, tenant API endpoints, and operator SSH bastion where permitted. Offline artifact testing allowed with signed artifact checks.
- Option C: Hybrid (edge + Redwood-hosted): test limited to customer edge gateway and tenant data in transit; Redwood-hosted control plane remains out of scope unless contractually approved.

Out-of-scope by default (unless explicitly listed):
- Redwood control plane (admin APIs, billing, multi-customer data stores)
- Redwood internal CI/CD and build infrastructure
- Third-party vendor consoles (cloud provider account plane)
- Live customer production tenants unless a specific production-acceptance addendum is signed

Permitted blast radius and safety gates:
- Timebox: maximum 72 hours of active testing per agreed window unless extended in writing.
- Rate limits: testers must not sustain request rates that cause service degradation above 5% of baseline latency at the tenant level; baseline is defined in pre-test synthetic run.
- Resource exhaustion prohibition: no deliberate GPU/host-level thermal or preemption attacks; discovery-only scanning for service identification is allowed under throttled settings.
- Authentication: where practical, pen-testers should authenticate as an end-user/service account provided by customer for tenant endpoints. Unauthenticated discovery must be pre-approved.

Pretest checklist (to be completed 7–14 days before):
1) Contract & NDA: signed mutual NDA and scope appendix.
2) Test plan: vendor sends stepwise test plan and tool list.
3) IP allowlist: customer and Redwood exchange IPs/CIDRs for test origin; operator firewall rules scheduled.
4) Target inventory: explicit list of hostnames, endpoints, ports, and tenant IDs.
5) Schedule windows: primary and fallback windows with oncall contacts.
6) Evidence escrow: agreed storage location (S3 bucket or secure upload), encryption key method, and retention period (default 90 days).
7) Rollback & safety procedures: operator-runbook reference and emergency stop/cutoff procedure confirmed.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Customer Security: provide target list, authenticate test accounts, confirm production/non-production status, and approve any expanded scope.
- Redwood Security (owner): authorize scope, review vendor plan, hold evidence escrow key, perform triage of findings, and publish remediation plan.
- Delivery/Field Ops: implement IP allowlists, schedule operator windows, and perform runbook remediation when required.
- Third‑party Tester: send pre-test plan, conduct tests within approved rules, produce reproducible findings with PoC, and deliver final report to evidence escrow.

Communication & escalation matrix:
- Primary on-call: eng-private-deployments oncall (pager: +1-555-0123, email: oncall-private@redwood.example)
- Security lead: Asha Patel (security) - asha.patel@redwood.example
- Customer technical lead: (customer-provided)
- Emergency stop procedure: immediate email + Slack @#private-deploy-ops, followed by firewall rule insertion to block test IPs.

Evidence and reporting requirements (minimum fields):
- Executive summary (1 page)
- Full findings list (CSV or JSON) with fields: finding_id, severity (critical/high/medium/low/info), affected_resource, reproducible_steps, PoC artifacts (curl commands, request/response captures), time_detected, remediation_recommendation, remediation_owner, verification_steps
- Raw pcap or request logs (when applicable), redacted to remove customer PII unless explicitly approved
- Signed attestations that no persistent backdoors or data exfiltration were left in place

Example findings CSV header (single-line example):
"finding_id,severity,affected_resource,summary,repro_steps,poc_artifact,time_detected,remediation_owner"

Remediation SLAs and verification:
- Critical: acknowledge within 2 hours, remediation plan within 24 hours, verification within 72 hours after fix applied.
- High: acknowledge within 8 hours, remediation plan within 3 business days, verification within 7 days.
- Medium/Low: acknowledge within 3 business days, remediation plan within 15 business days, verification according to priority.

Acceptance criteria for test completion:
- All critical findings mitigated or contained with agreed mitigation steps documented.
- High severity findings either remediated or have customer-accepted compensating controls and a cross-signed remediation timeline.
- Pen‑tester provides PoC or detailed reproducible step for every non‑informational finding.

Operator remediation playbook (condensed, stepwise):
1) Ingest finding into issue tracker (label: pen-test, customer: <customer-id>, severity).
2) Triage: reproduce in staging or isolated tenant where possible.
3) Contain: if immediate risk, apply temporary ACL/tenant isolation or disable affected endpoint.
4) Fix: apply code/config change, package as release candidate, run focused smoke tests (latency, correctness).
5) Deploy: follow customer-approved rollout (canary > 25% > 100% or tenant-swap).
6) Verify: run the verification steps provided in the finding, attach evidence to ticket.
7) Close: update remediation owner and dates, confirm customer and security sign-off.

Sample operator CLI snippets and artifacts to collect:
- Capture a tenant-level request trace (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token>" "https://tenant.example/api/v1/generate?model=gpt-XX" -D headers.txt -o body.bin
- Export runtime metrics for the test window:
  rctl metrics export --tenant <tenant-id> --start "2026-03-10T10:00Z" --end "2026-03-10T14:00Z" --out metrics.json
- Snapshot firewall rules before and after test windows (save as firewall-before.txt, firewall-after.txt)

Data handling and retention:
- All pen-test artifacts placed into the evidence escrow must be encrypted at rest using the agreed key. Redwood rotates escrow keys every 90 days; customer and vendor will be notified at least 7 days prior to rotation.
- Default retention for raw artifacts is 90 days. Summaries and remediation evidence are retained in Redwood issue tracker for 2 years.

Optional controls for risk-averse customers:
- Scoped read-only tests: limit to discovery and read operations; no authenticated destructive actions allowed.
- Staging-only: test only in a pre-production staging tenant with sanitized data.
- Time-bounded low-rate scans: allow only authenticated scans with strict rate caps.

Appendix A — Sample vendor attestation language:
"The testing firm certifies that all testing activities will be performed under the scope and constraints defined in the signed scope appendix. The firm will not retain persistent access or exfiltrate customer data. All artifacts will be delivered to the agreed evidence escrow and removed after the retention period unless otherwise requested in writing by the customer."

Appendix B — Common quick mitigations mapping (example table):
- Finding: unsecured metadata API -> Quick mitigation: restrict metadata endpoint to operator bastion CIDR and rotate service tokens.
- Finding: excessive tenant privileges -> Quick mitigation: revoke broad API keys, apply least privilege token and rotate keys.
- Finding: unauthenticated admin endpoints -> Quick mitigation: apply auth proxy with mTLS and block external routes.
